:::{#sol-transpose-product-practice}

No: the two [matrices](#def-matrix) differ,
so keeping the order of the factors gives the wrong [transpose](#def-matrix-transpose).

The [product](#def-matrix-mult) $\matr{A}\matr{B}$ and its transpose are

$$
\ba
\matr{A}\matr{B}
&= \begin{bmatrix}
1 \cd 1 + 2 \cd 1 & 1 \cd 0 + 2 \cd 1 \\
0 \cd 1 + 1 \cd 1 & 0 \cd 0 + 1 \cd 1
\end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(@def-matrix-mult)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix},
&& \text{(multiply and add)}
\ea
$$

so $\tp{(\matr{A}\matr{B})} = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$.

The transposes are
$\tp{\matr{A}} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$
and
$\tp{\matr{B}} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$,
so

$$
\ba
\tp{\matr{A}}\tp{\matr{B}}
&= \begin{bmatrix}
1 \cd 1 + 0 \cd 0 & 1 \cd 1 + 0 \cd 1 \\
2 \cd 1 + 1 \cd 0 & 2 \cd 1 + 1 \cd 1
\end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(@def-matrix-mult)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 \end{bmatrix}.
&& \text{(multiply and add)}
\ea
$$

Entry $(1, 1)$ is $3$ in $\tp{(\matr{A}\matr{B})}$ and $1$ in $\tp{\matr{A}}\tp{\matr{B}}$.
In the reversed order, as @thm-transpose-product says,
$\tp{\matr{B}}\tp{\matr{A}}
= \begin{bmatrix} 1 \cd 1 + 1 \cd 2 & 1 \cd 0 + 1 \cd 1 \\ 0 \cd 1 + 1 \cd 2 & 0 \cd 0 + 1 \cd 1 \end{bmatrix}
= \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$,
which matches $\tp{(\matr{A}\matr{B})}$.

:::
